claims: A mortgage broker is a licensed professional.
A mortgage broker acts as a middleman between homebuyers and lenders.
Mortgage brokers shop around 50–100+ lenders to secure the best rates and terms.
Mortgage brokers typically cost 1–2% of the loan amount if paid by the borrower or receive a lender commission.
Most commonly, the lender pays the mortgage broker a commission.
The lender commission is usually 0.50% to 2% of the total loan amount.
Lenders pay mortgage brokers a commission after the loan closes.
A broker fee is typically 1–2% of the loan principal.
Federal law generally caps broker fees at 3% of the loan amount.
Federal law requires broker fees not be tied to the interest rate.
Some banks only work directly with consumers.
Mortgage brokers are licensed through the Nationwide Multistate Licensing System (NMLS).
Mortgage brokers are required to be licensed.
Mortgage broker licensing includes completing pre-licensing education.
Mortgage broker licensing includes passing a written test.
Mortgage broker licensing includes passing background checks.
